December 14th, 2026, 10:00 A.M.

 

      NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN of teleconference public hearings, Monday December 14th, 2026, at 10:00 A.M. to be streamed live through the Boards website (www.nyc.gov/bsa), with remote public participation and in-person portion, on the following matters:

 

APPEALS  CALENDAR

2026-15-A

APPLICANT  Sheldon Lobel, P.C., for Anker Heegaard, owner.

SUBJECT  Application May 18, 2026  An administrative appeal challenging the Department of Buildings' final determination. The appeal challenges the DOB interpretation of the phrase 'existing floor space' in ZR Section 54-53 to include only lawful existing floor space in accordance with the provisions of the Zoning Resolution.  M1-2/R6, MX-8 Special Mixed Use District MX-8.         

PREMISES AFFECTED  330 Wythe Avenue, Block 2403, Lot 7501, Borough of Brooklyn.

COMMUNITY BOARD #1BK

 

2026-23-A

APPLICANT  Tatyana Artemova, for The West Side Tennis Club, owner.

SUBJECT  Application June 25, 2026  Appeal of a New York City Department of Buildings determination approving and issuing a Temporary Place of Assembly Certificate of Operations authorizing large-scale commercial concert use at Forest Hills Stadium.  R3-2 zoning district.         

PREMISES AFFECTED  1 Tennis Place/69-50 Burns Street, 101-02 Avenue/104-25  70 Road, Block 3219, Lot 1, Borough of Queens.

COMMUNITY BOARD #6Q

 

 

December 14th, 2026, and December 15th, 2026, 10:00 A.M. and 2:00 P.M.

 

      NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN of teleconference public hearings, Monday December 14th, 2026, at 10:00 A.M. and 2:00 P.M., and Tuesday December 15th, 2026, at 10:00 A.M. and 2:00 P.M., to be streamed live through the Boards website (www.nyc.gov/bsa), with remote public participation and in-person portion, on the following matters:

 

SPECIAL ORDER CALENDAR

 

789-45-BZVI

APPLICANT  Vassalotti Associates Architects, LLP, for Woodside 56, LLC, owner.

SUBJECT  Application September 29, 2026  Extension of Term of a previously granted Variance (§11-411) for the continued operation of a gasoline service station (Getty) which expired on July 13, 2026; Waiver of the Rules. M1-1 & R5 zoning district.

PREMISES AFFECTED  56-02 Broadway, 34-01 56th Street, 34-02 57th Street, Block 1185 Lot 44, Borough of Queens.

COMMUNITY BOARD #2Q

 

207-68-BZIII

APPLICANT  Gerald J. Caliendo, AIA, P.C., for Steve Green/Deerfield Meadows Inc., owner.

SUBJECT  Application July 17, 2026  Amendment to the Boards condition of term of a previously approved Variance (§72-21) which permitted the use manufacture and storage of paper vacuum bags, with accessory parking, which expired on June 18, 2023, Waiver of the Boards Rules.  R3-2 zoning district.       

PREMISES AFFECTED  115-58 Dunkirk Street, Block 10315, Lot 134, Borough of Queens.

COMMUNITY BOARD #12Q

 

173-78-BZII

APPLICANT  HSF Kramer (US) LLP, AREC 13, LLC, owner.

SUBJECT  Application October 9, 2026  Extension of Time to Obtain a Certificate of Occupancy of a previously approved Variance (§72-21) which permitted the storage, rental and sale of trucks and trailers with accessory motor vehicle repairs, and with parking, storage, and display in an open area contrary to underlying use regulations which expired on September 9, 2026.  C1-2/R5 and R5 zoning district.         

PREMISES AFFECTED  6607-6611 15th Avenue, a/k/a 6615-6645 New Utrecht Avenue, Block 5558, Lot 1, Borough of Brooklyn.

COMMUNITY BOARD #11BK

 

2016-4337-BZIV

APPLICANT  Eric Palatnik, P.C., for Joshua Schiller, owner.

SUBJECT  Application October 9, 2026  Extension of Time to Complete Construction and obtain a Certificate of Occupancy, of a previously approved Variance (§72-21) to permit the enlargement of an existing single-family home which expired on September 19, 2021, which expired on September 19, 2025, Waiver of the Boards Rules & Procedures.  R5 zoning district.         

PREMISES AFFECTED  127 Vanderbilt Street, Block 5264, Lot 51, Borough of Brooklyn.

COMMUNITY BOARD #7BK

 

2020-71-BZII

APPLICANT  Eric Palatnik, PC, for Strong River Properties, LLC, owner.

SUBJECT  Application October 29, 2026  Extension of Time to Complete Construction of a previously approved Variance (§72-21) to permit the development of a three-story single-family home which expired on October 3, 2026.  M1-1 zoning district.         

PREMISES AFFECTED  166 Coffey Street, Block 585, Lot 40, Borough of Brooklyn.

COMMUNITY BOARD #6BK

 

APPEALS  CALENDAR

 

2026-34-A & 2026-35-A

APPLICANT  Gerald J. Caliendo, for Harjit Singh/104-90 165 St. LLC, owner.

SUBJECT  Application May 4, 2026  Proposed development of a residential two-family building within the bed of a mapped street contrary to General City Law §35. R4 & R4-1 zoning districts.         

PREMISES AFFECTED  104-90 and 104-92 165th Street, Block 10163, Lot 90 and 100 Queens.

COMMUNITY BOARD #12Q

 

2026-36-A

APPLICANT  Rothkrug Rothkrug & Spector, LLP, for 93-08 150 ST LLC, owner.

SUBJECT  Application October 5, 2026  Proposed to develop the subject site with a 23-story mixed-use building located with the bed of a mapped street contrary to General City Law §35 and a waiver pursuant to ZR 72-01(g). C6-4 Special Downtown Jamacia Special Purpose District.         

PREMISES AFFECTED  93-02 & 93-08 150th Street, aka 149-16 Archer Avenue, Queens.

COMMUNITY BOARD #4Q

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN, PURSUANT TO LAW, that the following revocable consent has been schedules for a public hearing by the New York City Department of Transportation. A draft copy of the revocable consent agreement(s) may be obtained at no cost by submitting a request at diningoutnyc.info/requestcopy

The public hearing will be held remotely via Zoom, commencing on December 10th, 2026, at 11:00 am, in the matter of a proposed revocable consent authorizing the following:

  1. 11TH STREET HOSPITALITY to maintain, operate, and use a year-round roadway cafe for a term of four years adjacent to 314 W 11 Street in the Borough of Manhattan.

  2. VILLAGE SQUARE PIZZA III INC to maintain, operate, and use a year-round roadway cafe for a term of four years adjacent to 1200 Lexington Avenue in the Borough of Manhattan.

  3. G.V.S. BAKERY INC to modify a license issued to maintain, operate and use a sidewalk cafe for a term of four years adjacent to 36-21 Ditmars Boulevard in the Borough of Queens.

To join the hearing enter the following URL link into your browsers address bar: zoom.us/j/91467302621 Meeting ID: 914 6730 2621

To join the hearing only by phone, use the following information to connect: Phone: +1-929-205-6099 Meeting ID: 914 6730 2621

rows.additional_description_1:
Pursuant to Section 104 of the Public Officers Law, notice is hereby given of an open meeting of the Commissioners of the Civic Engagement Commission. Join the meeting to learn about programs and upcoming initiatives. 

 

The information for the meeting is as follows: 

Date: Wednesday, December 9, 2026 
Time: 6 PM  8 PM 

Location: 280 Broadway, New York, NY 10007  Enter at 53A Chambers Street 

 

Register To Participate in the Conversation 

The Commission will provide time for discussion related to civic trust, its mission, and activities. You may bring prepared comments to share during the meeting or submit written comments.  Please keep comments brief during the meeting (no more than three minutes). To allow for comments in an orderly fashion, please sign up in advance by emailing your name, and affiliation if appropriate, to info@civicengagement.nyc.gov or by texting or calling 917-587-9103?by 5 PM, Tuesday, December 8th. Participants who will be dialing in via phone are strongly encouraged to register in advance.  You may submit written comments during the meeting or via email to info@civicengagement.nyc.gov.  

 

Reasonable Accommodations 

You must contact the Commission if you need reasonable accommodation for a disability or language assistance. To request a sign language interpreter or to request free interpretation for Spanish and other languages, please contact the Commission no later than 5 PM, Wednesday, December 2nd by calling or texting 917-587-9103 or by e-mailing info@civicengagement.nyc.gov. Closed captioning is available. 

Para solicitar interpretación gratuita en español u otros idiomas, comuníquese con la Comisión a más tardar a las 5:00 p. m. del miércoles 2 de diciembre de 2026, llamando o enviando un mensaje de texto al 917-587-9103 o escribiendo a info@civicengagement.nyc.gov

PLEASE TAKE NOTICE that a public hearing will be held on December 9, 2026 at 10:00 a.m., or as soon thereafter as the matter may be reached on the calendar, at which time those wishing to be heard will be given an opportunity to be heard concerning the proposed disposition of the real property identified below. The public hearing will be held via conference call. Call in #: 1-646-992-2010; Access Code 717 876 299

Pursuant to Section 695(2)(b) of the General Municipal Law and Section 1802(6)(j) of the Charter, the Department of Housing Preservation and Development ('HPD') of the City of New York ('City') has proposed the sale of the following City-owned property (collectively, 'Disposition Area') in the Borough of Brooklyn:

 

Address                                     Block/Lot(s)

435 Locke Street                       4445/ 50     

1050 Ashford Street                   4446/ 1      

1 Gateway Dr                             4445/ 1      

                                                                       (Formerly Block 4445, p/o Lot 1 and Block 4446, p/o Lot 1)

              

 

Under HPD's New Construction Finance Program, sponsors purchase City-owned or privately owned land or vacant buildings and construct multifamily buildings in order to create affordable rental housing.  Construction and permanent financing is provided through loans from private institutional lenders and from public sources including HPD, the New York City Housing Development Corporation, the State of New York, and the federal government. Additional funding may also be provided from the syndication of low-income housing tax credits. The newly constructed buildings provide rental housing affordable to low- and moderate-income households, with at least 60% of units affordable to households earning up to 80% of Area Median Income (AMI) and up to 40% of units affordable to households earning up to 120% of AMI. At least 15% of units are set aside for formerly homeless households.

Under the proposed project, the City will sell the Disposition Area to Nehemiah Spring Creek 5B Housing Development Fund Corporation ('Sponsor') for the nominal price of one dollar per tax lot. The Sponsor will also deliver an enforcement note and mortgage for the remainder of the appraised value (Land Debt). The Sponsor will then construct three buildings containing up to 200 rental dwelling units, including one superintendent unit, on the Disposition Area.

The Land Debt or the Citys capital subsidy may be repayable out of resale or refinancing profits for a period of at least thirty (30) years following completion of construction. The remaining balance, if any, may be forgiven at the end of the term.

The appraisal and the proposed Land Disposition Agreement and Project Summary are available for public examination by emailing Margaret Carey at careym@hpd.nyc.gov on business days during business hours.

To make a request for accommodation, such as sign language interpretation services, please contact the Mayors Office of Contract Services (MOCS) via e-mail at disabilityaffairs@mocs.nyc.gov or via phone at (212) 298-0734.  TDD users should call Verizon relay services.  Any person requiring reasonable accommodation for the public hearing should contact MOCS at least three business days in advance of the hearing to ensure availability.

Under HPD's New Construction Finance Program, sponsors purchase City-owned or privately owned land or vacant buildings and construct multifamily buildings in order to create affordable rental housing.  Construction and permanent financing is provided through loans from private institutional lenders and from public sources including HPD, the New York City Housing Development Corporation, the State of New York, and the federal government. Additional funding may also be provided from the syndication of low-income housing tax credits. The newly constructed buildings provide rental housing affordable to low- and moderate-income households, with at least 60% of units affordable to households earning up to 80% of Area Median Income (AMI) and up to 40% of units affordable to households earning up to 120% of AMI. At least 15% of units are set aside for formerly homeless households.

Under the proposed project, the City will sell the Disposition Area to Nehemiah Spring Creek 5A Housing Development Fund Corporation ('Sponsor') for the nominal price of one dollar per tax lot. The Sponsor will also deliver an enforcement note and mortgage for the remainder of the appraised value (Land Debt). The Sponsor will then construct six buildings containing up to360 rental dwelling units, including one superintendent unit, on the Disposition Area.

The Land Debt or the Citys capital subsidy may be repayable out of resale or refinancing profits for a period of at least thirty (30) years following completion of construction. The remaining balance, if any, may be forgiven at the end of the term.

The appraisal and the proposed Land Disposition Agreement and Project Summary are available for public examination by emailing Margaret Carey at careym@hpd.nyc.gov on business days during business hours.

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the following matters have been scheduled for public hearing by Community Board:

BOROUGH OF THE BRONX

COMMUNITY BOARD NO. 3 - Tuesday, December 8, 2026 at 6:00 PM, Children's Circle Day Care Center, 1332 Fulton Avenue, Bronx, NY

A Public Hearing on ELURP Application: HPD 260002PPX, 1388-1400 Stebbins Avenue  (HPD ELURP) The Stemma

The Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) seeks ELURP approval for disposition of city-owned property to facilitate a twelve-story approximately 115,106 zoning square foot building with a total of approximately 152 affordable housing units, plus one additional unit for a superintendent, and a community facility space the proposed development.  The proposed development will be developed on a currently City-owned site located at 1388-1400 Stebbins Avenue (Block 2965, Lots 6, 7, 8, and 13) the proposed development site in the Crotona Park East neighborhood of Community District Three, Bronx.

HPD proposes the following action to facilitate the Proposed Development: Disposition of the City-owned Development Site to a sponsor selected by HPD that is organized exclusively to develop housing projects for persons of low income. 

The Public Hearing will take place prior to the General Board Meeting. 

The proposal can be accessed on the Zoning Application Portal (ZAP): 

https://zap.planning.nyc.gov/my-projects/to-review

If you would like to submit a written testimony, please e-mail eritter@cb.nyc.gov no later than Monday, December 7, 2026, 5:00 P.M. end of business day.

rows.additional_description_1:
NOTICE OF A FRANCHISE AND CONCESSION REVIEW COMMITTEE (FCRC) PUBLIC HEARING to be held on 12/7/2026, at 2:30PM at 255 Greenwich Street, 8th Floor, New York, NY 10007 relative to the proposed amendment of the Public Communications Structures franchise agreement between the City of New York and CityBridge, LLC.

The proposed amendment would extend the term of the franchise agreement to March 22, 2035, while also amending various other terms, including a modification to the minimum number of structures that must be deployed and an increase of the minimum fee due to the City of New York.

The public may participate in the public hearing by attending and providing testimony. Written testimony may be submitted in advance of the hearing electronically to fcrc@mocs.nyc.gov. All written testimony must be received by 12/7/2026.

 

A draft copy of the proposed franchise agreement amendment may be obtained at no cost any of the following ways:

  1. Submitting a written electronic request to the NYC Office of Technology and Innovation (OTI) at franchiseopportunities@oti.nyc.gov from 11/20/2026 through 12/4/2026.
  2. Downloading from 11/20/2026 through 12/7/2026 on OTIs website. To download a draft copy of the proposed franchise agreement amendment, visit https://www.nyc.gov/content/oti/pages/franchises.
  3. By submitting a written request by mail to NYC Office of Technology & Innovation, 2 MetroTech Center, P-1 Level Mailroom. Written requests must be received by 12/4/2026. For mail-in requests, please include your name, return address, and a request for a specific calendar item.

 

The agenda and related documentation for the hearing will be posted on the MOCS website at https://www.nyc.gov/site/mocs/opportunities/franchises-concessions.page. 

 

For further information on accessibility or to make a request for accommodations, such as sign language interpretation services, please contact the Mayors Office of Contract Services (MOCS) via e-mail at DisabilityAffairs@mocs.nyc.gov or via phone at (212) 298-0800. Any person requiring reasonable accommodation for the public hearing should contact MOCS at least five (5) business days in advance of the hearing to ensure availability.

A draft copy of the revocable consent agreement(s) may be obtained at no cost by submitting a request at diningoutnyc.info/requestcopy

The public hearing will be held remotely via Zoom, commencing on December 3rd, 2026, at 11:00 am, in the matter of a proposed revocable consent authorizing the following:

  1. C&K Grocery Corporation to modify a license issued to maintain, operate, and use a sidewalk cafe for a term of four years adjacent to 362 2 Avenue in the Borough of Manhattan.

  2. AURORA FG INC to modify a license issued to maintain, operate, and use a year-round roadway cafe for a term of four years adjacent to 362 2 Avenue in the Borough of Manhattan.

  3. MANSIONS OF GLORY HOSPITALITY LLC to maintain, operate and use a year-round roadway cafe for a term of four years adjacent to 53 Spring Street in the Borough of Manhattan.

  4. SHOO SHOO EAST LLC to maintain, operate and use a year-round roadway cafe for a term of four years adjacent to 1477 2 Avenue in the Borough of Manhattan.

To join the hearing enter the following URL link into your browsers address bar: zoom.us/j/91467302621 Meeting ID: 914 6730 2621

rows.short_title: NYCHA Audit and Finance Committee Meeting.
rows.additional_description_1:
The next Audit & Finance Committee Meeting of the New York City Housing Authority is scheduled for Thursday, December 3, 2026, at 10:00 A.M. in the Ceremonial Room on the 5th Floor of 90 Church Street, New York, New York. Copies of the Agenda will be available on NYCHAs Website or may be picked up at the Department of Internal Audit and Assessment at 90 Church Street, 9th Floor, New York, NY, no earlier than twenty-four (24) hours before the upcoming Audit & Finance Committee Meeting. Copies of the draft Minutes are available on this web page or can be picked up at the Department of Internal Audit and Assessment no earlier than 3:00 P.M. on Thursday, two weeks after the Audit & Finance Committee Meeting.

Any changes to the schedule will be posted here and on NYCHAs website at https://www.nyc.gov/site/nycha/about/audit-committee-meetings.page to the extent practicable at a reasonable time before the meeting.

The meeting will be streamed live on YouTube Channel and on NYCHA's Website, at https://www.nyc.gov/site/nycha/about/audit-committee-meetings.page for public access.

The meeting is open to the public.  For those wishing to provide public comment, pre-registration is required, at least 45 minutes before the scheduled Committee Meeting. Comments are limited to the items on the Agenda.

Speaking time will be limited to three minutes. Speakers will provide comments in the order in which the requests to comment are received. The public comment period will conclude upon all speakers being heard or at the expiration of 30 minutes allotted for public comment, whichever occurs first.

Any person requiring a reasonable accommodation in order to participate in the Audit & Finance Committee Meeting should contact the Department of Internal Audit and Assessment by phone at 212-306-3441 or by e-mail at audit@nycha.nyc.gov, no later than Friday November 27, 2026, 5:00 P.M.

For additional information regarding the Audit & Finance Committee Meeting, please visit NYCHA's Website, contact by phone, at (212) 306-3441, or by email, at audit@nycha.nyc.gov

rows.short_title: Bronx Borough President Public Hearing Notice  ELURP Application: HPD 270002 PPX  1605 Nelson Avenue (HPD ELURP)
rows.additional_description_1:
A VIRTUAL PUBLIC HEARING IS BEING CALLED by the President of the Borough of The Bronx, Honorable Vanessa L. Gibson. This public hearing will be held on Tuesday, December 1, 2026 commencing at 10:00 a.m.  The public hearing may be accessed virtually using the link provided:

 

https://bit.ly/1605Nelson

Meeting ID: 271 492 632 764 742 

Passcode: Ks7pN7hE

 

Or call in: 646-561-8032

Conference ID: 468 601 675#

 

Please submit any written testimony to: publictestimony@bronxbp.nyc.gov. Written testimony will always be accepted, but only testimony received by Friday, December 4th will be considered for the Borough Presidents recommendation.

 

APPLICATION NO: HPD 270002 PPX  1605 Nelson Avenue (HPD ELURP)

 

IN THE MATTER OF an application submitted by the Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) pursuant to Section 197-e of the New York City Charter for the disposition of city-owned property located at 1605 Nelson Avenue (Block 2876, Lot 55) to facilitate an affordable housing project, Borough of The Bronx, Community District 5.

 

The full proposal can be accessed on the Zoning Application Portal: https://zap.planning.nyc.gov/projects/2027X0226

 

Please direct any questions concerning this hearing to the Office of The Bronx Borough President: bxbpplanning@bronxbp.nyc.gov.

rows.additional_description_1:
Design Commission Special Meeting Agenda

Monday, November 30, 2026

 

 

Meeting Location: Public Design Commission meetings are being held in-person at the Public Design Commission Board Room on the 3rd Floor of City Hall. Members of the public can either attend in-person or view the meeting remotely. The entrance to City Hall, the restrooms, and the meeting rooms are wheelchair accessible.

 

The meeting will be livestreamed on the Public Design Commissions YouTube channel at http://www.youtube.com/nycdesigncommission.

 

 

Public Meeting

 

2:30 p.m.        Motion to Vote

30623:                Construction of a gaming facility, resort, retail, and events complex (Integrated Resort), as part of the master plan for the Metropolitan Park (Queens Future), north of Roosevelt Avenue, between Grand Central Parkway and Seaver Way, south of the Worlds Fair Marina, and adjacent to Citi Field, Flushing Meadows Corona Park, Corona, Queens. (Preliminary and Final) (CC 21, CB 3, 4, 6, 7, 8 & 9) EDC/DPR

 

https://www.nyc.gov/assets/designcommission/downloads/pdf/pres/11-16-26-EDC-DPR-pf-QF-IntegratedResort.pdf

 

Items on the Motion to Vote agenda are not presented. The public testimony for item #30623 has been heard and is now closed.

 

All times are approximate and subject to change without notice, and those who are viewing remotely should follow along on the livestreamed meeting on the Design Commissions YouTube channel to know when to join the meeting. If attending in-person, please plan to arrive early in the event the meeting is ahead of schedule.

 

Do you need assistance to participate in the meeting? If you need a reasonable accommodation of a disability, such as translation into a language other than English; American Sign Language Interpreting (ASL); Captioning in Real-Time (CART);

or the meeting agenda in Braille, large print, or electronic format, please contact the Public Design Commission at least as soon as possible before the meeting.

 

Public Design Commission
City Hall, Third Floor
Phone: 212-788-3071
Fax: 212-788-3086

www.nyc.gov/designcommission

designcommission@cityhall.nyc.gov

rows.short_title: Bronx Borough President Public Hearing Notice  C 240216 ZMX  4506 Park Avenue Rezoning
rows.additional_description_1:
A VIRTUAL PUBLIC HEARING IS BEING CALLED by the President of the Borough of The Bronx, Honorable Vanessa L. Gibson. This public hearing will be held on Monday, November 30, 2026, commencing at 10:00 a.m.  The public hearing may be accessed virtually using the link provided:

APPLICATION NO: C 240216 ZMX  4506 Park Avenue Rezoning

https://bit.ly/4506Park

Meeting ID: 250 736 099 852 022 8

Passcode: 6RK9PL36

 

Or call in: 646-561-8032

Conference ID: 353 613 502#

 

Please submit any written testimony to: publictestimony@bronxbp.nyc.gov. Written testimony will always be accepted, but only testimony received by Tuesday, December 1st will be considered for the Borough Presidents recommendation.

IN THE MATTER OF an application submitted by Rocky & Brothers Realty LLC pursuant to Section 197-c and 201 of the New York City Charter for the amendment of the Zoning Map, Section No. 3c:

1. changing from an R6A District to an R7A District property bounded by a line 100 feet northeasterly of East 182nd Street, Washington Avenue, East 182nd Street, and a line midway between Park Avenue and Washington Avenue;

2. changing from an M1-1 District to an R7X District property bounded by East 183rd Street, a line midway between Park Avenue and Washington Avenue, East 182nd Street, and Park Avenue; 

3. establishing within the proposed R7A District a C2-4 District bounded by a line 100 feet northeasterly of East 182nd Street, Washington Avenue, East 182nd Street, and a line midway between Park Avenue and Washington Avenue; and

4. establishing within the proposed R7X District a C2-4 District bounded by East 183rd Street, a line midway between Park Avenue and Washington Avenue, East 182nd Street, and Park Avenue; 

as shown on a diagram (for illustrative purposes only) dated September 9, 2026, and subject to the conditions of CEQR Declaration E-937.

 

Related Application: N 240217 ZRX

 

The full proposal can be accessed on the Zoning Application Portal: https://zap.planning.nyc.gov/projects/2023X0146

 

Please direct any questions concerning this hearing to the Office of The Bronx Borough President: bxbpplanning@bronxbp.nyc.gov.
